title: Density Ratio by Temperature and Altitude
description: Density ratio curves for 0, 2,500, 5,000 and 7,500 ft against airstream temperature (0-1,000°F) with a movable marker, followed by five challenges that ask for a density ratio or a standard-air catalog pressure before the chart marks the point.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: standard air
barometric pressure
air density
density ratio
hot airstream
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Correcting fan performance for temperature and altitude with the density ratio
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the air density ratio for a given airstream temperature and site elevation, to within ±0.01, and use it to convert a required pressure into a standard-air catalog pressure.

accessibility.notes: Native range input, select, text input and buttons; the marker readout is a live text line under the chart; verdicts and each new challenge announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs, circle/square marks and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the four curves differ by dash pattern as well as colour; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge.

controls.label: Density ratio / Pressure
controls.purpose: Type the answer to the current challenge

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clear the marks and the score and repeat the challenges

equations: catalog pressure = required pressure / density ratio
rules: Ratios shown to three decimals; density to four
Density ratio answers correct within ±0.01, pressure within ±0.05 in. wg; two attempts
Marker, elevation and hover readouts locked while a challenge is open
assumptions: Dry air; barometric pressure from the standard atmosphere at each elevation
limitations: Humidity and weather changes in barometric pressure are ignored
Only the four tabulated elevations are offered

sources: Density ratio equation and the 0.075 lb/ft³ standard: Chapter 2, 'Standard Air'
Barometric pressures: Chapter 2 elevation table, computed from the standard atmosphere
Challenge 5: Chapter 2, 300°F oven exhaust worked example

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore the shape of the correction, then calculate values the chart confirms only after the answer is committed
keyQuestions: Why must °F be converted to °R (add 460) before dividing?
Why is the ratio at 600°F exactly half the ratio at 70°F?
Going from the job to the catalog, do you multiply or divide by the density ratio?
commonMisconceptions: Temperature in °F can be used directly in the ratio without adding 460
Hot air raises the pressure a fan develops
To find the catalog pressure, multiply the required pressure by the density ratio
Altitude and temperature corrections cannot be combined
assessmentOpportunities: End score shown as 'n of 5 correct on first attempt'; mastery is 4 of 5 on the first attempt.
